data.final_week_advice: Week 4 is the final week before the exam. Focus on timed practice and reviewing the specific equilibrium concepts covered in the live class. Ensure you can solve net ionic equations and stoichiometry problems quickly, as these are high-yield for the free-response section.
data.summary: This four-week plan prioritizes foundational units (1-4) in the first half to build necessary chemical literacy. Units 5-9 are introduced in the second half, with a dedicated live class for Equilibrium in Week 4. The final week is reserved for mixed review and timed practice to simulate exam conditions.

weeks.focus: Mastering atomic structure and basic stoichiometry
tasks: Complete 10 practice problems on molar mass and mole conversions (1.1).
Analyze 3 mass spectra to determine elemental composition (1.2, 1.3).
Write electron configurations for 10 elements and identify valence electrons (1.5, 1.8).
Solve 5 stoichiometry problems involving limiting reactants (4.5).

weeks.focus: Understanding bonding, intermolecular forces, and gas laws
tasks: Draw Lewis structures and VSEPR shapes for 12 molecules (2.5, 2.7).
Rank 5 substances by boiling point based on intermolecular forces (3.1).
Solve 8 ideal gas law problems including partial pressures (3.4).
Write net ionic equations for 6 precipitation and acid-base reactions (4.2).
Calculate reaction rates and determine rate laws from experimental data (5.1, 5.2).
Perform calorimetry calculations for 3 endothermic/exothermic processes (6.4).
Calculate pH for 5 strong and weak acid/base solutions (8.2, 8.3).
Design a buffer solution and calculate its pH (8.4).

weeks.focus: Equilibrium review and full exam simulation
tasks: Attend live class on Equilibrium (7.1) and take detailed notes.
Calculate Kc and Q for 5 reversible reactions (7.3, 7.4).
Complete a 90-minute timed practice exam covering all units.
Review incorrect answers from the timed exam and re-do 3 free-response questions on thermodynamics (9.3).
